narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which evaluated your financial profile and determined a 63% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a level of uncertainty high enough to result in a denial of your application. While no single factor sealed this outcome, three aspects of your profile carried the most weight in this decision, and understanding them may help you take meaningful steps forward.

The most influential factor was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. This was the strongest signal the system picked up on, and it pushed the assessment firmly toward concern. Among applicants who were approved, only about one in five had a negative checking account balance, while the majority either had no account or maintained a positive balance. A negative balance suggests that your day-to-day finances may be under strain, which raises questions about your ability to take on additional monthly obligations.

The duration of your requested loan — 24 months — also contributed to the denial, though to a lesser degree. Approved applicants received loans with an average duration of around 19 months, so your request for a longer repayment period signals a higher exposure window for the lender. Longer loan terms mean more time during which financial circumstances could change, and the system interpreted this as an added layer of risk in your case.

Interestingly, the amount you requested — 1,659 DM — actually worked in your favor. This is notably lower than the average loan amount of around 2,887 DM among approved applicants, and the system recognized this as a positive signal, partially offsetting some of the concern raised by your account status and loan duration. Unfortunately, this positive factor was not strong enough to outweigh the others.

Beyond these top three factors, your profile also includes a history of past payment delays and a short employment tenure of less than one year, both of which are less common among approved applicants and likely added background pressure to the overall assessment. Your housing situation — renting rather than owning — and your job classification as an unskilled resident also place you in groups that are underrepresented among those who were approved.

As a next step, we strongly encourage you to work on stabilizing your checking account balance and, if possible, building a track record of consistent, on-time payments over the coming months. Securing more stable employment and allowing more time to pass in your current role could also meaningfully improve your profile. When you feel ready to reapply, consider whether a shorter loan term might better fit your current financial situation, as this could reduce the perceived risk. Speaking with a financial advisor about strategies to strengthen your credit standing before reapplying would be a worthwhile investment in your future application.
